prompt:
Return exactly one bare JSON object with all five keys: name, phone, email, company, country. Values are strings or JSON null. No prose, fences or additional keys. Normalize only the single contact block in the user's note.

Critical precedence: A country supplied by the country line wins over a different calling code in the phone, and an international phone keeps its written calling code. When country is missing, infer it from a uniquely assigned international calling code; shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave it null. This is the only exception to leaving missing fields null. A national phone without a country is null.

Extract and assign:
- Use only the record's Label<sep>value lines, which may have variable labels, variable separators (colon, equals, tab) and shuffled order. Ignore surrounding notes and signatures. Trim values and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Absent lines, empty values and these whole-value placeholders in any case are missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.
- Assign email to the value containing @, regardless of label. Assign phone to the value with at least seven digits made only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and an extension. Strip extensions of the forms ext. N, ext N, xN, #N, extension N, with N representing digits.
- Use the country line for country, subject to the exception above. If the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not, swap those two values. Use the suffix list below. Do not infer fields from a domain, suffix or non-record text.

Normalize country and phone together:
- Country is uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German country names and alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes, case-insensitively. Map UK and Great Britain to GB, Holland to NL, USA and U.S.A. to US, Türkiye to TR, Czech Republic to CZ.
- With tel: and extension removed, test for a leading + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. For international numbers, turn 00 into +, delete (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the calling code as written and apply the country precedence above.
- For national numbers, remove formatting separators and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the normalized record country's calling code. Output non-null phones as E.164: + followed by calling-code and national significant digits only.

Normalize the other fields:
- Email: strip mailto: and surrounding < > and lowercase the whole address. Preserve the source characters apart from these operations; do not correct it to match a name, a company or a domain guess.
- Name: split at the first comma and turn Last, First into First Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof (optional dot, any case). For each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase its first character and lowercase the rest. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate.
- Company: remove a trailing legal suffix, case-insensitively, with its optional preceding comma: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. For each space-separated word, uppercase its first character and lowercase the rest.
